newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines attract more Asian rice suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Philippines attract more Asian rice suppliers.

text.p: Asian rice exporters continue to woo the Philippines which has embarked on a rice procurement programme, officials at the Philippine Agriculture Department said on Monday.
The latest batch of prospective rice sellers to Manila include Malaysia, India and Pakistan, they said.
Malaysia and India had offered to supply up to 100,000 tonnes of rice each to the Philippines, a senior official at the department told Reuters.
Last week, Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said state-owned National Food Authority was negotiating with two Pakistani rice suppliers to buy more rice.
Agriculture officials said NFA may not likely tap the Indian rice market due to a "bad experience in the past."
The official did not elaborate but traders said the supplies from India had not met quality standards. NFA had imported rice from India in the past two years.
President Fidel Ramos has authorised the NFA to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice before the onset of the seasonally thid quarter lean season.

NFA has so far clinched deals for the supply of 205,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand. It has also signed separate contracts for the supply of 100,000 tonnes each from China and Vietnam, with an option to buy an additional 100,000 tonnes each from both countries.

Grains traders had earlier expressed doubts on the capability of China to export such volumes to the Philippines, but officials of the Agriculture Department said the contract stipulated China can souce the commodity from Thailand, Vietnam and even Pakistan.
NFA deputy administrator Gregorio Tan said NFA has kept all negotiations on the country's rice imports so as not to stir up rice prices in the region.
NFA also denied any anomalies on its rice importations.

Early today, Tan denied in an interview with radio station DZRH tNFA bought "overpriced" rice from Vietnam in answer to reports that Vietnam rice was being traded around $235 per tonne FOB against the $291.50 C&F clinched by the NFA.
"Even if it's true that you can buy rice at $235 per tonne FOB, you are not sure that you can bring out the rice because the Vietnamese rice market is a regulated market," Tan said.

Tan said the NFA signed a contract with Vietnam Food Corp at the time the price of Thai rice was trading at $304 to $310 per tonne. The Thai rice market is used as a benchmark for Asian rice prices, he said.
NFA bought the Chinese rice also at $291.50 per tonne C&F and the Thai rice at $300 per tonne C&F.

Tan said the NFA negotiated with a state owned company of Vietnam to import rice to ensure immediate supply before July this year. "During the years between 1992 and 1995, private and provincial government units in Vietnam had inked export commitments with other countries but were unable to effect deliveries," he said.
NFA said it expects bulk of its rice imports to arrive between March 1 and June 30 this year, in time for the traditional lean months of July to September.

The NFA said is also set to take delivery of 12,738 tonnes of U.S. rice on March 7 which was contracted last year under Title 1 of the U.S. government's PL 480 programme. Title 1, also known as the Food for Peace Programme, is a loan programme for the purchase of farm goods with low interest rates and long-term payback periods.
